definitions.explanation: Something given to someone, especially for a special occasion.

examples.japanese: {誕生日|たんじょうび}の{贈|おく}り{物|もの}を{買|か}った。
これは{友達|ともだち}からの{贈|おく}り{物|もの}です。
examples.english: This is a gift from a friend.

examples.japanese: {贈|おく}り{物|もの}をきれいに{包|つつ}んでもらった。
examples.english: I had the gift nicely wrapped.

examples.japanese: {母|はは}の{日|ひ}の{贈|おく}り{物|もの}には、いつも{花|はな}を{選|えら}んでいる。
examples.english: For Mother's Day gifts, I always choose flowers.

examples.japanese: {思|おも}いがけない{贈|おく}り{物|もの}をもらって、とてもうれしかった。
examples.english: I received an unexpected gift and was very happy.

notes:
{贈|おく}り{物|もの} means 'gift' or 'present.'

Formation: {贈|おく}る (to give as a gift) + {物|もの} (thing)

Similar words:
- {贈|おく}り{物|もの} vs. プレゼント: プレゼント is more casual and modern; {贈|おく}り{物|もの} is more formal/traditional
- {贈|おく}り{物|もの} vs. お{土産|みやげ}: お{土産|みやげ} specifically refers to souvenirs brought back from trips

Common collocations:
- {贈|おく}り{物|もの}をする: to give a gift
- {贈|おく}り{物|もの}を{選|えら}ぶ: to choose a gift
